Title: Vitae paparum Avenionensium, hoc est Historia pontificum romanorum qui in Gallia sederunt ab anno Christi MCCCV usque ad annum MCCCXCIV, Stephanus Baluzius magnam partem nunc primum edidit, reliquam emendavit ... Nouvelle édition revue d'après les manuscrits et complétée de notes critiques par G. Mollat
Creator: Étienne Baluze (1630-1718), editor of the Lives; new edition by G. Mollat (born 1877)
Publisher: Paris: Librairie Letouzey et Ané
Publication Date: 1921
Rights: Public Domain
Rights basis: the title page of this scan reads 'PARIS LIBRAIRIE LETOUZEY ET ANÉ ... 1921' and the 'Nihil obstat' is dated 23 January 1921 (read in the OCR); the item record gives 1914 and possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT; the volume is a French publication of 1921, before 1931.
Language: lat (mixed: Latin lives of the Avignon popes with Mollat's French preface and notes)
Source: Internet Archive item vitaepaparumave00balugoog (archive.org/details/vitaepaparumave00balugoog), full-text file vitaepaparumave00balugoog_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the Library thread, October 2026.
Provenance note: Header prepended by the Library thread; the OCR text follows unchanged apart from this header. Nothing stripped, normalised, corrected, re-spaced or retyped. Latin and French sampled at opening, middle and end: readable, with scattered letter errors. The Google boilerplate pages are left at the head. The host lists a second scan (vitaepaparumave04balu) and other volumes of the set; only this volume, which holds the Latin Lives, is vendored.
Content note: The Lives of the Avignon popes, Clement V (1305) to Gregory XI and the Schism's first years (to 1394), from the contemporary lives gathered by Baluze, with Mollat's corrected text. Contemporary court and chronicle voices on the Avignon papacy; some lives were written by papal chaplains or Avignon clerics, and the volume prints letters of the popes inside the lives. The notes and the 'collectio actorum veterum' are in the companion volume and are not vendored.
